title: operational-metrics-cadence-and-observability-kanban-notes
content:
Purpose:

This doc captures a proposal for an operational cadence and lightweight Kanban to manage metric definitions, tracing budgets, and dashboard gating with a focus on keeping DB/query costs predictable while preserving investigation velocity for inference incidents. This is intended as a working plan for Q3 instrument sprints and the observability ops rotation.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to production inference telemetry across hosted, dedicated and private control-plane signals.
- Does NOT change existing SLI definitions; it proposes a cadence for reviewing/curating and gating dashboards, probes and trace sampling.
- Priority: keep incident mean time to resolution (MTTR) stable while reducing query/trace storage spend by ~15% over 3 months.

Background / Motivation:
- We’ve accumulated a ton of dashboard panels and high-cardinality metrics. Query costs and noisy alerts are making oncall triage slow.
- Observability teams are seeing spiky trace ingestion during fanout-heavy requests (multi-model routing) and during rollout events.
- Need a lightweight continuous process (not a big rename project) to prune, gate, and prioritize signals with owners.

Key goals (measurable):
- Reduce median dashboard query cost by 20% for the top 30 operator dashboards within 90 days.
- Keep P95 investigation latency within current bounds (no more than +10% change).
- Establish per-team trace sampling budgets and a simple fallback policy for capacity spikes.

Proposed cadence (roles and frequency):
- Weekly "Observability Kanban" sync (30 min): review new instrumentation PRs, accept/triage probe proposals. Owners: obs-product lead + rotating eng-observability representative.
- Biweekly metrics review (60 min): owners present changes, retirement proposals, and cost impact estimates. Owners: metric owners.
- Monthly trace-budget retro (45 min): evaluate sampling budgets, real spend vs allocation, adjust guardrails. Owners: SRE + applied-ml rep.
- Quarterly dashboard audit: cull stale panels and reassign ownership; produce a lightweight deprecation list. Owners: dashboard steward roster.

Metric tiering and gating rules:
- Tier 0 (Safety / SLO): must-have, 90-day retention, high-cardinality allowed. Example: request_success_rate, model_error_rate.
- Tier 1 (Operator-critical): 60-day retention, limited cardinality. Used on operator consoles and critical runbooks.
- Tier 2 (Product/analytics): 30-day retention, sampled or aggregated. Suitable for notebooks and ad-hoc queries.
- Tier 3 (Experimental / ad-hoc): ephemeral, 7–14 day retention, incubating metrics; default sampling/rollup.
- Gate for new Tier 0/1 metrics: requires cost estimate and owner; must pass Kanban triage.

Synthetic probe matrix (compact):
- Probe: "latency-synthetic-end-to-end" -> SLI: end-to-end P95 latency -> Frequency: 1m for global probe, 30s for narrow-region probe -> Alert: P95 > SLO by 20% for 3 consecutive checks -> Cost class: low (small synthetic agents).
- Probe: "kv-warmth-check" -> SLI: kvcache hit ratio -> Frequency: 5m -> Alert: drop > 10% sustained 10m -> Cost class: tiny.
- Probe: "model-fanout-tail-check" -> SLI: tail token-latency per route -> Frequency: 1m -> Alert: P99 spike > baseline*2 -> Cost class: medium (requires trace samples).

Trace sampling and budget rules:
- Baseline policy: 5% sampling for regular production traffic, 25% for errors and high-latency requests (auto-flagged).
- Tenant weighting: allocate sampling percentage proportional to weekly CPU token usage. Top N tenants get a minimum sampling floor to preserve debugging signal.
- Dynamic backpressure: if trace ingestion exceeds 80% of budgeted daily bytes, progressively reduce non-error sampling (to 1%) and increase error-only sampling.
- Fallback behavior: route high-fidelity traces to archival tier for 30 days (replayable), keep indexes minimal.

Dashboard gating and slimming heuristics:
- Panels per dashboard target: 8–12 primary panels; extras move to collapsed sections or a secondary tab.
- Widget cost score = query_cost_estimate * frequency_multiplier (dashboard refresh freq). Prefer panels with low estimated cost or cached transforms.
- Gate new dashboards that query raw logs > 1M rows/day: require aggregation view or precomputed rollup table.
- Encourage use of pre-aggregated SLO tables and rolling counters instead of broad GROUP BY on high-cardinality tags.

Ownership and handoff playbook:
- Every dashboard and metric must have an explicit owner and a fallback owner. Ownership metadata lives in the dashboard description and in the metrics roster spreadsheet.
- On rotation week, oncall takes responsibility for surfacing obvious noisy panels and filing quick deprecations (label: obs-deprecate).
- Decommission path: 1) owner proposes deprecation in Kanban, 2) 2-week warning window via slack channel, 3) archive panel -> delete after 30 days if no objections.

Kanban board structure (minimal columns):
- Backlog: ideas and audit items.
- Triage: requires decision on tier/cost/owner.
- In progress: agreed changes.
- Validation: deployed, monitoring cost impact (2 weeks).
- Done / Archived.

Short-term tactical checklist (8-week runway):
1) Run cost-aware query for top-100 dashboard panels (Diego) -> produce per-panel cost estimates.
2) Populate metric roster with owners and tier recommendations (Priya).
3) Implement trace ingestion budget dashboard and alarm at 75% (SRE).
4) Add gating rule to instrumentation PR template: cost estimate + intended tier (obs-tooling PR #219).
5) Pilot dashboard slimming on 3 operator dashboards; measure query cost before/after.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Granularity of tenant weighting: should we use weekly token spend or last-30d? Pros/cons written in notes below.
- Archive vs precompute: for which panels is it worth building a rollup table vs archiving traces? Need engineering estimate.
- How to incorporate private deployments (on-prem) where trace storage cannot be centrally managed? Proposal: provide a minimal local retention default and a config guide.

Notes to self / meeting snippets:
- "If we can shave infrequent high-cost panels we’ll get 40% of savings with 10% of work" — initial estimate during sprint planning.
- Keep the Kanban lean; the weekly 30m cadence tends to be the most effective (too many meetings kills progress).

References / links for reviewers:
- Confluence working draft: https://confluence.redwood/team/obs/cadence-playbook
- Instrumentation PR template (obs-tooling): https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-tooling/pull/219
- Related Jira: JIRA-OBS-4827 (dashboard audit), JIRA-OBS-4930 (trace-budget dashboard)

Action items for this doc:
- Reviewers: please comment on the proposed tier boundaries and sampling fallback plan by 2025-08-08.
- Diego: run panel cost query and attach CSV to the Kanban card.
- Priya: start owner outreach for Tier 0/1 metrics next week.

End of notes.

(Informal style intended — this is a working plan, not a finalized policy.)
